title: Notifications Technical Reference
readerIntent: Use the stable module, API, model, Pipeline, provider, event, Axis, and verification contracts.
priorKnowledge: Read the overview, configuration, operations, and security pages.
summary: Reference for extending and operating the Notification capability while preserving owner boundaries and replaceability.

sections.heading: Modules and authority
items: gNotify is composition-only. notifySchema owns private persistence models; notifyCore owns provider-neutral orchestration; notifyVerification owns challenges; notifyApi owns secured transport routes; provider modules own vendor behavior.
Business capabilities own intent and value builders. Profile/Customer owns preference evidence. Workflow owns human/long-running recovery. Axis owns presentation only.

sections.heading: Private models
items: Channel, scenario, message type, delivery policy, template, immutable template version, variable definition, provider, provider account, message context evidence, delivery request, delivery attempt, suppression, in-app notification, verification challenge.
Generated routers are disabled. Domain services and interceptors guard lifecycle mutation and prohibit hard deletion of evidence.

sections.heading: Routes
items: Service-only send and retry; access/service verification create/validate; access-only test-send, provider-account governance, diagnostics, preview, publish, retire, rollback, inbox and acknowledge. Every route is secured, token-scoped, permissioned, and uses explicit Controller → Facade operations.
Customer modules replace services or contribute later routes/metadata through normal layering; do not expose a generic invoke operation or generated delivery CRUD.

sections.heading: Delivery Pipeline
items: validateRequest, resolveScenario, resolveChannel, resolveRecipientAndConsent, resolveTemplate, resolveContext, renderContent, selectProvider, persistRequest, sendMessage, normalizeResult/failure, persistAttempt/suppression, publishEvent, end.

Exact duplicate idempotency terminates before provider delivery. Retry uses a separate bounded Pipeline and business-owned context rehydration. Human approvals and uncertain long recovery use Workflow.

sections.heading: Provider contract
items: Minimum input: request/channel/recipient reference, selected account, transient rendered channel content, stable idempotency, deadline. Minimum output: normalized status/result/failure, safe provider reference, retry classification, latency and bounded evidence.

Production adapters require explicit activation, secret reference, readiness, timeout, rate/retry/fallback, idempotency, callback/reconciliation behavior, observability, recovery, environment tests and rollback.

sections.heading: Verification commands
items: Run focused gNotify contracts and persisted runtime journeys; combined Notification/KYC/Order suites; npm run llm:generate then npm run llm:validate; structure audit and basic backend tests; nodicsaxis verify/build; nodicsdocs verify; explicitly enabled environment/provider/topology tests.
Generated metadata, static source inspection, fake transports, or green unit tests never substitute for the environment-backed portions of production qualification.

Record exact commands, environment identity, selected provider/account, fixtures, outcomes, failures and recovery evidence. Re-run after configuration, adapter, policy, template, permission, topology, secret, framework, Axis, or documentation changes.
